summary: Inconsistent idempotency scope across SDKs for multiplexed batch streaming causing duplicate tool executions after partial reconnect
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports duplicate downstream tool (payment webhook) invocations after a client-side network blip during a multiplexed streaming session. Impact: duplicate payments sent to their payment processor for ~0.5% of streamed requests over a 3-hour window. Environment: Dedicated cluster in us-east, Python SDK (v1.8.3) producer, TypeScript SDK (v2.0.1) consumer, model gptx-2-large.

Observed behavior: OnyxPayments uses a batching pattern where a single streaming connection carries multiple parallel tool call requests (multiplexed). When a client reconnect occurs and the SDK resends unacknowledged batch frames, the Python SDK injects a per-action idempotency token (action_id) but also includes a per-stream idempotency header. The TS SDK's reconnect logic only replays the original request body without reattaching the per-action token, leading the service to treat the replay as new for some actions. Result: downstream tool executed twice for a subset of actions.

Why this is urgent: Customer handles financial transactions; duplicates lead to reconciliation overhead and potential regulatory exposure.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a multiplexed streaming session from SDK-A (Python v1.8.3) to Redwood Hosted endpoint with 8 parallel logical requests over one TCP stream.
2) Trigger a sequence of actions that include a tool/function call invoking an external payment webhook (sandbox).
3) Simulate a transient network disconnect that drops the TCP connection after the server has accepted some frames but before all action acks are returned (client later reconnects).
4) Allow SDK reconnect and replay of unacknowledged frames. Observe webhook receiver and Redwood request logs for duplicate invocations.
logs: Excerpt from gateway logs (us-east-1) showing two executions for action_id 'act_7f3a' across two different request IDs: req-20260312-01 and req-20260312-01-r2. Timestamp delta: 00:00:07. Trace IDs: trace-8b2a and trace-9c3b. See attached full dump in internal link.
investigation_notes: Initial triage: confirmed duplicate external webhook posts correlated with client reconnect window. No server-side retries configured for this route.

Reproduced in lab with SDK matrix: Python v1.8.3 (producer) + TS v2.0.1 (consumer) with intentional disconnect -> duplicates observed. When both endpoints use Python SDK or both use TS SDK, behavior differs: duplicates reproduced only when producer SDK attaches per-action idempotency differently than replaying SDK.

Hypothesis: idempotency token normalization and placement differ across SDK implementations. Service expects a single canonical idempotency key per action; if absent or mismatched on replay, server treats as new action.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:42 - Aditi Sharma: Customer reports ~120 duplicate payments in a 3-hour window after a deploy. They provided webhook logs and example request IDs.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Jonah Park: Assigned. I've requested packet captures and SDK telemetry from the customer. Asked for exact SDK versions and whether they use any proxies or load balancers.

2026-03-12 11:18 - OnyxPayments (customer): Provided pcap and streaming session trace. Confirmed they use a sidecar proxy but it preserves headers; they also confirmed they perform per-action UUID generation client-side.
2026-03-12 14:02 - Jonah Park: Reproduced in internal staging. Created GH issue and PR to unify idempotency header normalization across SDKs (see related PR).

2026-03-13 08:30 - Eng (runtime): Noted that the serving runtime accepts both per-stream and per-action keys but de-duplication table TTL is 30s. If reconnect replay occurs after TTL, duplicates happen. Suggest increasing TTL for routes marked as 'external-side-effect'.

2026-03-13 12:10 - Support: Coordinating a short-term mitigation: recommend customer enable explicit per-action idempotency propagation on reconnect and enable 'strict-idempotency' flag in their Dedicated config.
2026-03-13 16:45 - Customer: Agreed to apply workaround and run for 24 hours; requested timeline for SDK patch.
resolution: Workaround applied: OnyxPayments enabled explicit per-action idempotency resend on reconnect and toggled strict-idempotency at the route level; duplicates stopped in the monitoring window. Engineering changes: SDK team to release Python and TS patches that standardize idempotency header naming and ensure per-action tokens are preserved on replay. Runtime change: evaluate increasing de-duplication TTL for routes marked as external-side-effect. Follow-ups: INT-1124 created to track SDK release and runtime config change; postmortem to be published in confluence after implementation.
